title: Q2 Roadmap Blueprint — Synchronized release lanes for Hosted API and Model Catalog phasing
creator: Nadia Patel
description:
Objective: Produce a concrete Q2 blueprint that aligns Hosted API endpoint rollouts with model-catalog phasing so we can reduce cross-team friction, avoid double releases, and guarantee rollback/fallback coverage for high-risk endpoints.

Success metrics: (1) all scheduled Hosted API releases have an explicit compatible model variant or fallback (target: 100%), (2) mean time between rollout regressions < 7 days, (3) number of cross-team blockers reduced by 50% compared to Q1.

Scope IN: release lane definitions, canary schedules, gating criteria (performance & eval thresholds), per-release owner roster, cross-team runbook, observable dashboards for rollout-level metrics.
Scope OUT: infra capacity procurement contracts (handled by ENG procurement), long-term model lifecycle policy (separate PM initiative).

Sequencing / Release lanes:
- Green lane: low-risk model tweaks and non-breaking API changes (1-week canary).
- Amber lane: quantization/latency improvements requiring integration tests (2-week canary + perf SLO validation).
- Red lane: model family swaps, architecture changes, or any change that can alter output semantics (4-week staged canary + human eval checkpoint).

Gating criteria (per-lane):
- Unit + integration tests: pass
- Latency/throughput: within 10% of baseline for green/amber, within 15% for red
- Quality regression: no statistically significant drop on canary prompt set (A/B with n>=200 prompts)
- Cost delta: expected per-token cost increase flagged to finance if >15%

Canary schedule template (example):
- Day 0: internal-only smoke + infra checks
- Day 1-3: 1% traffic, automated eval + perf monitoring
- Day 4-7: 5-10% traffic, deploy canary cohort, manual review if amber/red
- Day 8+: 50%+ ramp depending on signals; automatic rollback on fail

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Whether to allow model quantized variants as primary in green lane (trade-off: cost savings vs evaluation surface complexity). PM prefers enabling quantized variants for beta customers; eng requests a short validation window. Action: Marcus to propose a validation checklist by 2026-03-22.
- Default canary durations for amber lane (2 vs 3 weeks). Decision leaning toward 2 weeks with extended telemetry retention.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: overlapping model rotations causing client-visible regression. Mitigation: enforce per-customer release windows and require explicit dependency mapping in release ticket.
- Risk: insufficient eval coverage for niche prompt classes. Mitigation: add targeted evals from top 10 enterprise customers; SEs to surface sets by 2026-03-24.

- Canary runbook (drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/rdw-canary-playbooks
- Reference PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pulls/template/release-pr.md
